environment.postgres: PostgreSQL server 18.0-2; server_version_num=180000; isolated database symphony_phase1_test
environment.database_role: symphony owner role; no app-role/RLS claim

claims.behavior_proved: PostgreSQL tests prove identical concurrent command replay has one committed effect; a rolled-back owner permits one contender; concurrent reuse of a receipt key with changed actor, command type, or semantic envelope is denied without disclosing the stored result or committing losing aggregate effects; competing expected-version writes do not overwrite newer state; retries apply only to SQLSTATE 40001 and 40P01 for at most three total transaction attempts, including an uncertain-commit re-entry, with the same command identity; commit-boundary uncertainty resolves from a separately pooled fresh connection, re-enters only after a healthy lookup confirms no receipt, and returns an outcome-neutral retryable result when lookup fails.
claims.path_proved: The PostgreSQL command bus, receipt store, aggregate repository, events and outbox were exercised against isolated symphony_phase1_test. WP1.3 concurrency integration passed 12 tests; WP1.2 command/audit regression passed 9 tests; domain unit tests passed 87 tests; workspace typecheck, architecture verification, and the Phase 1 contract gate passed. All green gates ran with Node 26.7.0/npm 12.2.0 and PostgreSQL 18.0 (package build 18.0-2).
claims.configuration_proved: Node v26.7.0, npm 12.2.0 for all green gates, PostgreSQL server_version_num=180000, database symphony_phase1_test, role symphony, DATA_MODE=test, deterministic local HMAC test keys, and a separately pooled Kysely recovery client were used. MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL was derived in-process from the existing local DATABASE_URL credentials by changing only the database path; no credential or connection string was logged or persisted. The retained pre-implementation red run used the npm.cmd 11.19.0 fallback after the sandbox denied the user-scoped npm launcher; it is chronology evidence, not a green gate.
coverage_limitations: Commit loss is exercised with narrow pre-commit and post-commit fault hooks at the transaction boundary; the test does not sever a live network socket during PostgreSQL's COMMIT exchange.

The current test database still uses its legacy session app.current_tenant_id RLS policy. The isolated fixture initializes that legacy setting on test connections while the command runner sets app.tenant_id transaction-locally. No least-privilege app-role or WP1.5 RLS claim is made.

BDD-AUD-002/003 HTTP composition and public response assertions belong to WP1.6. Terminal VERSION_CONFLICT receipt/inbox atomicity belongs to WP1.4; tenant RLS belongs to WP1.5; mutable-authority revocation races belong to WP2.4.

The tests-first log records the intended pre-implementation retry and uncertain-commit failures; that initial run also exposed a test-fixture double-close cleanup issue, corrected before the passing run.
